{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the fish concept and sketched it on the pad. The design had a split at the nose, a top and bottom curve around the body, and a flared tail. It used only gentle curves, so a single push could run through it, and the table adopted it right away. I laid the bottom line (stroke 2) from the nose to the tail, about 40 dominoes in several passes. In the last minute I laid the four dominoes that carried the bottom line into the tail flare. By my read of the table, about 101 of the 108 standing dominoes would fall, and the outline reads clearly as a fish.

Execution: I fetched a tray-load early so I could start building immediately, and I traced my stroke directly from the pad so the shape matched the plan. I inspected the nose, the bottom line and the join area repeatedly, and I gave concrete advice on the tight turn at the flare: carry the line on right for a few dominoes, then bend down gently. I finished the join in time and called hands-off before the push.

Collaboration: I assigned the strokes clearly (top line to Jack, bottom line to me), told Omar and Hana what to watch, and kept the table informed about what I was working on. I stayed out of others' areas to avoid bumps and asked for the same in return. I also made sure the start domino went to whoever traced stroke 1.

Leadership: I set the direction in the first minute, chose a simple animal whose outline reads on its own, split the work so no one was idle, and kept the group focused on one full check of the fall as the clock ran down. I called the final hands-off so nothing was disturbed before the push.", "my_share_percent": 35}
